answer.answer: Conservative answer: it cannot be confirmed from the supplied sources that Delta Queue reliably guarantees exactly-once delivery. What the sources establish is: (1) the Delta Queue documentation describes exactly-once delivery — this is the documented claim (delta-doc); (2) an incident report records that during incident DQ-17 some messages were delivered twice — direct evidence that the documented guarantee was violated in at least one observed case (delta-incident). What changed: an incident (DQ-17) demonstrated duplicate delivery, contradicting the documented claim. What is current: the only current documented position available states exactly-once delivery (delta-doc), but its currency relative to the incident is unknown. What remains historically valid: DQ-17's duplicate deliveries occurred as recorded (delta-incident). What is unresolved: whether the guarantee holds today depends on information not supplied — snapshot timestamps, root cause, and remediation status. Treating documented claims as unverified against observed behavior, a conservative assessment is that exactly-once delivery should be treated as a documented claim with at least one evidenced violation, not as a confirmed operational guarantee.
